processing: A partly oxidised oolong finished as plump, tight strips; the details of each step are not widely recorded and are presumably close to other Guangdong strip oolongs.
harvest_season: Exact seasons are not well recorded; as with most Guangdong oolongs, spring is the usual prized picking.
appearance_dry: Plump, tight, smooth and even strips, yellowish brown with an oily sheen.
appearance_liquor: Orange-yellow and bright, leaning slightly golden.
appearance_wet: Typical of strip oolong: long leaves that open fully.
taste_profile: A high, natural floral and honey scent over a mellow, clean, smooth cup with a good sweet return.

brewing.notes: Keep the early steeps short to hold the high floral note; water just off the boil suits strip oolong.

vintage_note: Usual for an aromatic oolong: sold as the current year's harvest and best drunk fresh, since the floral scent is its main appeal. It is not known as an ageing tea. Ask for the year and season, and look for the geographical indication when buying under this name.
description:
Xi Yan Oolong comes from Xiyan Mountain in Dabu County, Meizhou, in northeastern Guangdong, a misty range whose main peak reaches about 1,256 m. It is a young tea by Chinese standards and carries a geographical indication.

The gardens are described as high on the slopes of the mountain, in Fenglang town, with plenty of cloud and yellow-red soil. The finished leaf is a plump strip with a yellowish brown, oily look.

In the cup it goes for scent: high florals and honey, then a clean, mellow body and a sweet finish. As with other aromatic strip oolongs, hot water and short early steeps keep the perfume and avoid bitterness.

It is sometimes listed among the notable teas of Guangdong, though it is far less seen abroad than Fenghuang Dancong. Buy it as recent harvest and from someone who can say where on the mountain it was grown.
history:
The tea was created in the late 1970s, so it belongs to the modern wave of Guangdong oolongs rather than to an old tradition.

Its reputation was built through competitions: it is reported to have won a Guangdong famous tea gold award in 1994, a gold at the second China Agricultural Expo in 1995, and a gold at the fifth Zhongcha Cup in 2003.
